conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ve been reviewing your case. You’re here because of severe epigastric pain, nausea, and vomiting that started three days ago. Is that right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, that’s correct. It started like a stomach bug—nausea, vomiting, even diarrhea—but now the pain is constant and I can’t keep anything down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. And you’ve had similar episodes before, related to your chronic pancreatitis. This looks like another flare-up, what we call acute on chronic pancreatitis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it feels just like last time. But I couldn’t get an IV in the ER—my veins are tough. They gave me shots for pain and nausea.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s why we went ahead and placed a central line. It’s a midline in your right arm, so we can give you fluids, medications, and make sure you’re comfortable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, okay. I saw the bandage. Is it safe? I’ve had blood clots before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we placed it carefully. We avoided your left side because of your history of DVT. This one is in your right brachial vein and should be low risk.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I’m just worried about another clot.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re monitoring that. For now, we’re giving you IV fluids, pain meds like Dilaudid, and anti-nausea medication. You’ll stay NPO—nothing by mouth—for a while to let your pancreas rest.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: How long will I be here?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Usually a few days. We’ll start you on liquids once the pain and nausea improve, then slowly advance your diet.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. My blood pressure was high in the ER—was that from the pain?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Very likely. We’re continuing your lisinopril and amlodipine. We also have clonidine available if it stays elevated.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my other meds—like seroquel, amitriptyline, tramadol? I haven’t taken them since I got sick.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re holding those for now since you can’t take pills. But once you can eat, we’ll restart them. No changes planned—we’ll go back to your usual doses.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I get anxious when I miss them.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll give you lorazepam as needed for anxiety. And we’ll keep an eye on your mood. You’re not having any thoughts of harming yourself, are you?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, not now. I’ve been stable. Just want to feel better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s good to hear. We’ll check in daily. Rest now—we’ll keep you comfortable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How’s the pain today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Still there, but a little better. Nausea is less.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s progress. We’re going to try a small amount of clear liquid later—water or broth—if you’re up for it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’d like to try. I hate being on IVs.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll start slow. Also, your liver tests were high when you came in, but they’re already trending down, which is a good sign.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that from the pancreatitis?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s common during flares. They should normalize as you improve.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You did well with the clear liquids yesterday. Today, we’d like to try a soft diet—like toast or applesauce. How do you feel about that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m willing to try. My stomach feels calmer.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. We’ll start small and watch for any nausea or pain. Also, we’re switching your stomach protection from IV pantoprazole back to your regular omeprazole by mouth.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I take that every day.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, and we’ll restart your Creon with meals to help digest food, since your pancreas isn’t producing enough enzymes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I forgot about that. I need those with every meal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well—tolerating soft foods, pain is down. We’re going to try a regular diet today, maybe some eggs or rice.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Really? That’s great. I’m so tired of liquids.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, but we’ll still go slow. Also, we checked a stool test for C. diff since you had diarrhea at the start. It came back negative, so no infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I had that before. Glad it’s not back.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve been eating regular meals without issues. That’s a big step. We’ve restarted all your oral meds—tramadol, amitriptyline, seroquel, lamictal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I already feel more like myself. My mood is better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. We’re also watching your potassium—it was low earlier, so we’re giving supplements. It’s improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I didn’t know it was low. Could that make me weak?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, exactly. We’re correcting it, so you should feel stronger soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We did a chest X-ray to check your midline. The tip is in the right place—upper SVC. No issues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s safe to keep using it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, until discharge. We’ll remove it before you go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re up and walking around—great to see. Your belly is less swollen and much less tender.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel stronger every day. When can I go home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: If you keep this up, probably in a couple of days. We want to make sure you’re eating well and pain is controlled with oral meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: All your labs are normal now—liver tests, potassium, everything. You’re doing really well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. I was worried about my liver.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No sign of complications. Your pancreatitis is resolving. We’ll keep the midline for now but plan to remove it tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Today we’ll remove the midline. You’re eating regular food, pain is mild, and you’re managing meds by mouth.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Will it hurt?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a little pressure. We’ll clean the site and put a bandage. You’ll be fine.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Midline is out. Site looks clean. You’re one step closer to discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve made great progress. Another day of observation, and if all goes well, you can go home tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m ready. What do I need to do after I go home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Keep taking all your medications as prescribed—especially Creon with meals, omeprazole, and your pain and mental health meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And if I get pain again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Use your tramadol as needed. If pain is severe or you can’t keep fluids down, come back. Also, follow up with your PCP and specialists.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you for helping me through this.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing so well. We’re discharging you today. You’re alert, eating well, and your vitals are stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great news. I feel ready.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll send you home with all your meds. Keep your follow-ups with GI, psychiatry, and your pain specialist.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I have them scheduled. I’ll take care of myself.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve worked hard. Call us if anything changes. Safe travels home.
